name: WorkMate.Base
description: Runs on every new tenant before anything customer-specific. Edition recipes and sector packs layer on top; they never replace it.
author: Aramis Enterprise Solutions
$notes: The six steps of specification section 3, in order.
Steps carrying a $stub property are placeholders for a module that has not shipped its recipe step yet. Each names the module that will own it. A test asserts that no $stub step survives its module.

Feature ids are verified against the pinned Orchard Core version with tools/api-probe --features. OrchardCore.Search.Lucene and OrchardCore.Search.Elasticsearch are marked obsolete in 3.0.1; OrchardCore.Lucene is the current id (ADR-0004).
This file is the source of truth. Directory.Build.targets copies it into the host's content root at build, which is where Orchard's ApplicationRecipeHarvester looks.

steps.$comment: Step 1 of 6. Enable the platform features and the entitled module features. HCM modules are not here: they are an entitlement decision and arrive through an edition recipe.
steps.name: Feature

steps.$comment: Step 1 of 6, continued. Select the themes. A theme takes two things and both are easy to miss: its feature has to be enabled, in the step above, and it has to be selected, here. Enabling without selecting leaves the admin with no layout; selecting without enabling leaves the theme's shapes unavailable and Orchard falls back to the admin theme, which has no front-end Layout shape, so every front-end page throws - including /Login, and nobody can sign in at all. Section 3: 'The admin theme is Orchard's, extended with a WorkMate layout'. TheTheme is a placeholder for the site: the employee and manager surfaces become a front-end theme in WorkMate.Hcm.SelfService, and these two lines change to name it.
steps.name: themes

steps.$comment: Step 2 of 6. Create the six platform roles. PermissionBehavior is Add on every role, deliberately: the default is Replace, which would make an edition recipe layered on top wipe these grants rather than add to them. Every permission name here is pinned by PermissionNameTests against the constant that declares it in the pinned version, because the Roles step ignores a name it does not recognise without saying so. Each module grants its own permissions through a PermissionStereotype when its feature is enabled, so this list never has to name another module's. ManageRoles is Platform Administrator only until product decision 2 settles who configures a customer; Tenant Administrator can assign existing roles to users but not edit role definitions.
steps.name: Roles

Roles.Name: Platform Administrator
Roles.Description: The delivery team. Configures the tenant, including features and deployment.

Roles.Name: Tenant Administrator
Roles.Description: The customer's own administrator. Configures the business, not the platform.

Roles.Name: HR Administrator
Roles.Description: Runs human capital administration. Its permissions arrive with the HCM modules.

Roles.Name: Manager
Roles.Description: Sees and approves for their own part of the organisation.

steps.$comment: Step 3 of 6. Default site settings and the two cultures every tenant has. WorkMateSettings defaults to Bahrain because the first tenants are there; a tenant elsewhere overrides it in its own recipe or on the settings screen.
steps.name: Settings

$comment: Step 4 of 6. The system dimension types every tenant starts with.
CostCentre only. It is the one kind of unit the platform itself refers to — payroll, cost
allocation and the GL reference on every record all mean the same thing by it — so a tenant
that has not defined it is a tenant those features cannot describe. Division, Department and
the rest are deliberately absent: what a customer calls their levels is theirs to decide, and
a base recipe that guessed would leave every tenant deleting three types before starting.
Re-running is safe per ADR-0008: an identical row is skipped, a divergent one fails naming
the difference rather than overwriting what the customer has since changed.
pluralEn/pluralAr/menuOrder are the Organisation menu entry, per ADR-0024. The plural is
AUTHORED, never derived: the per-dimension menu shipped once with a guessed plural and was
withdrawn because it read Branchs in English and had no Arabic plural at all. A type with
no authored plural falls back to its singular, which is short and never wrong.
menuOrder 90 puts Cost centre after the organisational levels (Business Unit 10,
Division 20, Department 30, ...) and before anything a customer invents, which lands
unordered at 0 and sorts by name.
GRADE is added by slice F5+F7 (decision D26 C). It is NOT an organisational level and so
does not breach the rule above: a grade is a level WITHIN a position, it never appears on
the organisation tree, and shipping it guesses nothing about how a customer describes their
company. Its menuOrder 70 puts it just before Cost centre.
role: Grade is how the product FINDS this dimension — the employee form's grade drop-down
and a position's allowed-grades picker both ask for the type whose role is Grade. Declared
here rather than guessed from the code or the name, because the demo recipes ship
zenith-grade and because FRS Rule 6 lets a customer rename Grade to Band without thereby
losing the drop-down. See DimensionTypeRole.
There is NO grade-step type. D26 C removes the step level that D5 and D7 described: a
position's allowed grades ARE its levels. A tenant that wants a heading above SE-1..SE-3
creates an ordinary Grade value and uses the grade > grade diagonal on the grades axis
below, which is a grouping and not a level.
steps.name: dimension-types

$comment: POSITION. The post an employee holds — D20: Position, Job title and Designation are
one concept, always Position. role: Position is how the employee form's position
drop-down and a grade picker find it; see DimensionTypeRole for why a code or a name
cannot be read instead.
nameAr is the indefinite singular منصب, like every other type here (إدارة, فرع), and the
plural carries the article. D26 A writes the label as المنصب; that is the definite form
a sentence uses, and StandardDimensionPlurals — frozen by ADR-0009 — keys منصب.
ApprovedHeadcount is an ATTRIBUTE rather than a field on DimensionRecordPart, because
that part is carried by every generated dimension content type and a Division does not
have a headcount. Not required: absent means 1 (D26 E), which is the common case of a
post held by one person. Attributes are undated, so 'what was the approved headcount
last March' is not answerable — D15, a stated limitation and not an oversight.
Position is NOT added to the organisation structure's levels. ADR-0028: where a
position sits in the business is the customer's shape to declare, so they add it to
their own chart. Until they do, a position can report to another and has nowhere in the
business to sit, and the Add form says exactly that.
Step 4 of 6, continued. The primary organisation axis, deliberately empty.
No levels, no root types and no containment: every new tenant gets an organisation chart to
fill in, not one somebody else guessed at. The designer renders an empty structure correctly
— the structure card with nothing under it — and the Structures editor is where the customer
names their own levels and ticks what may sit under what.
isPrimaryOrganisation makes this the default scope for approvals and data visibility, which
is a decision about which axis is authoritative rather than about its shape, so it is safe to
take here. A Cost structure is NOT created: see the module README for why that is a customer
decision rather than a platform one.
THE GRADES AXIS IS NOT AN EXCEPTION TO THAT RULE, and ADR-0028 says why in full. A grade
ladder is not the customer's organisation chart: it has exactly one level, it carries no
units, nothing rolls up through it, and no employee is placed on it. Shipping it guesses
nothing about the company and is what makes Organisation > Grades usable on a new tenant
without somebody first having to invent an axis for it. What is still NOT shipped is any
grade VALUE and any place for Position on the organisation chart.
grade > grade is ticked so a tenant MAY group its grades - an SE heading above SE-1..SE-3,
decision D26 C. The shipped data is flat; the diagonal only means the tenant is allowed to
do it, which is the one thing a step concept would have decided for them.
employeeAttachableTypeCodes is deliberately absent rather than stated as []: an empty list
means UNCONSTRAINED, not 'nothing may hold employees', so stating it would read as a
restriction while being none. Nothing ever writes an assignment on this axis, which is what
actually guarantees no employee is placed on a grade.
steps.name: structures

$comment: THE REPORTING LINE. ADR-0028: a position needs two parents at once — its unit in the
business (FRS figure 9) and the position it reports to (FRS 4.1.4) — and D19 gives a
value exactly one parent PER AXIS. So they are two axes, which is the mechanism ADR-0005
scoped links to a structure for, and neither tree knows about the other.
position > position is the whole containment: a reporting line is positions all the way
down. Every position may be a root, because the CEO reports to nobody.
NOTHING IS EVER PLACED HERE. An assignment names the structure it is on, and employees
are placed at positions on the ORGANISATION axis, so no headcount rolls up a reporting
line — which is the point. 'How many people are under the COO' and 'how many are in
Corporate' are different questions and must not share a number.
employeeAttachableTypeCodes is absent rather than [] for the reason given on the grades
axis: empty means unconstrained, so stating it would read as a restriction while being
none.
Step 5 of 6. The managed lists a form field offers as choices: job title, grade,
employment type, work location, document type, nationality, country, currency,
relationship and contact type.
Applied by reference rather than inline, deliberately. The same lists have to reach a
tenant created today and one created before slice B2, and the second can only get them by
applying the file by hand from Configuration > Recipes - so there is one file and this
names it, rather than two copies that drift. ADR-0008's lookup-list addendum is what makes
applying it to a tenant that already has the lists safe: a missing entry is added, an
entry that differs fails naming the difference, and a customer's own entries are left
alone.
Before form-definitions because a field binding names a list by code, and the list should
exist before anything offers it.
steps.name: recipes

steps.$comment: Step 5 of 6, continued. Create the standard content types every tenant has.
steps.name: form-definitions

steps.$comment: Step 6 of 6. Install the standard report library.
steps.name: reports
